source: NHS - Heart attack; AHA warning signs
text: Chest pain or pressure that spreads to the arm, jaw or back, with sweating, nausea or shortness of breath, may be a heart attack. Call emergency services immediately; do not drive yourself.
Sudden face drooping, arm weakness, slurred speech, sudden confusion, vision loss or severe sudden headache suggest stroke. Act FAST: call emergency services at once.

topic: breathing difficulty shortness of breath wheeze
text: Severe breathlessness at rest, inability to speak in full sentences, blue lips, or breathing that is rapidly worsening needs emergency care. Mild breathlessness with a cough or cold can start with a GP or urgent care visit.

topic: severe allergic reaction anaphylaxis swelling throat hives
text: Swelling of lips, tongue or throat, wheezing, widespread hives or fainting after an allergen exposure may be anaphylaxis. Use an adrenaline auto-injector if prescribed and call emergency services.

topic: heavy bleeding wound bleeding won't stop
text: Bleeding that soaks through dressings or does not stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure needs emergency care. Apply direct pressure and keep the person still.

topic: fever in infant baby child high temperature
source: NHS - High temperature in children; CDC
text: A fever in a baby under 3 months, or a fever with rash that does not fade under a glass, stiff neck, drowsiness or difficulty waking needs urgent same-day assessment or emergency care. Older children with mild fever can often be managed with rest, fluids and a pediatrician call.

source: NHS - Stomach ache and abdominal pain
text: Severe or worsening abdominal pain, especially localized to the lower right side, with fever, repeated vomiting or a rigid belly needs urgent assessment. Vomiting blood or black stools needs emergency care.

source: NHS - Head injury; CDC HEADS UP
text: After a head injury, loss of consciousness, repeated vomiting, seizure, worsening headache, confusion or clear fluid from the nose or ears needs emergency evaluation.

topic: suicidal thoughts self harm mental health crisis
source: NHS - Urgent mental health help; 988 Lifeline
text: Thoughts of suicide or self-harm, or a feeling of being unable to stay safe, need immediate support: call or text 988 (US) or emergency services, and stay with a trusted person. Do not leave the person alone.

topic: cough cold sore throat flu mild symptoms
source: CDC - Flu symptoms and care; NHS - Common cold
text: Mild cough, sore throat, runny nose or low fever usually improve with rest and fluids. Book a GP visit if symptoms last more than 10 days, or earlier for high-risk people (older adults, pregnancy, chronic illness).

Signs of dehydration include very dark urine, dizziness, dry mouth and not passing urine for 8 hours or more. Seek urgent care if unable to keep fluids down, if blood is present, or for infants and older adults.

source: NHS - Pregnancy warning signs; CDC Urgent Maternal Warning Signs
text: Vaginal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, severe headache with vision changes, or reduced baby movement in pregnancy needs same-day maternity or emergency assessment.

topic: back pain numbness leg weakness bladder
source: NHS - Back pain (cauda equina red flags)
text: Back pain with numbness around the groin, new bladder or bowel control problems, or progressive leg weakness is a red flag needing emergency care. Ordinary back pain without these signs can be seen by a GP or orthopedics.
A spreading red, hot, painful patch of skin with fever needs same-day assessment. Stable, non-painful rashes can be booked with a dermatologist or GP.
